newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - July 24.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Thursday:
Irish Independent
- Irish pound headed for 87 pence sterling as exchanges sell mark
- Norwich figures show Irish unit's new business up 23 percent at 10 million punts
- Donegal Creameries plans to present flotation proposals to its board within five weeks
- Relaunch for The Title newspaper planned
- First Maryland is strong but card debts still rising
- Elan posts $40 million for second quarter
- 50,000 new jobs forecast but punt slide may hit prices
- Three christian brothers and one former brother appeared in court in Galway on a total of 51 sex abuse charges
- Inflation fears as Irish pound hits new lows
- Governments stand firm on Northern Ireland talks deadline
- Irish students face UK third level education fees
- Currency troubles could restrict finance minister Charlie McCreevy's options for tax cuts
- Sterling is at the highest level in eight years
- First Maryland profits held back by credit card losses
- EU questions tax status of certain areas of enterprise
- Greenspan ripples keep Irish stocks buoyant as U.S. sets pace
The Examiner
- Economic boom to turn dole into jobs with 50,000 jobs to be created this year
- GAA fined 13,000 punts as judge says thousands could have been poisoned because of a lack of hygiene at a Croke Park stand
- Unionist rejection of disarmament plan casts doubts on future of North peace
